display.title: Sukkos Farbrengen in Mineola, NY: The Alter Rebbe and the Miser's Nickel
display.summary_short: At a Sukkos farbrengen on the day of Moshe Rabbeinu, a guest speaker teaches the power of seeing the good, with the story of the Alter Rebbe, a captured groom and a miser's rusty nickel.
display.summary_long: A guest speaker at a community Sukkos farbrengen in Mineola, New York, greets the crowd and his old yeshiva study partner, the host rabbi. Today's Ushpiz is Moshe Rabbeinu, and he tells how Moshe proved himself a leader as a shepherd by gently carrying a runaway lamb back to the flock. He explains that 'negative' is 'neged tov', the opposite of good, and that we should focus on the good. Then comes the story: on the wedding day of two orphans, an antisemitic police chief seizes the groom for 25 years in the army and demands 1,500 rubles. The Alter Rebbe arrives, collects from a poor community, and insists on going first to 'Moshe the miser', who for years has given only one rusty nickel. The Alter Rebbe accepts the nickel with a heartfelt blessing, and Moshe, moved to tears, explains how a beggar once threw that nickel back at him, then gives the whole sum. The groom is freed and the wedding goes on; that night the police chief is killed in a riding accident, and the groom finds the ransom money, which the rabbi gives to the couple. The speaker urges everyone to see the good in themselves and others, make peace, and build the unity that brings Moshiach.
display.lesson: Look for the good in every person, including yourself; accepting even a small good deed warmly brings out much more, and unity brings Moshiach.

advisories.note: An antisemitic police chief seizes a groom on his wedding day to draft him for 25 years and threatens the townspeople with Siberia.
